# Unit test for function evalString
def test_evalString() -> None:
    cases = [
        ("''", ""),
        ('"hello"', "hello"),
        ("'''line 1\nline 2'''", "line 1\nline 2"),
        ('"""line 1\nline 2"""', "line 1\nline 2"),
        (r"'\a\b\f\n\r\t\v'", "\a\b\f\n\r\t\v"),
        (r"'\\\'\"'", "\\'\""),
        (r"'\x00\x41\xff'", "\x00A\xff"),
        (r"'\101\377'", "A\xff"),
        (r"'\1234'", "S4"),
        (r"'\x414'", "A4"),
        (r"'\q'", r"\q"),  # Unknown escapes are preserved.
        (r"'It\'s fine'", "It's fine"),
        (r'"say: \"hello\""', 'say: "hello"'),
    ]

    for literal, expected in cases:
        assert evalString(literal) == expected

    # repr() output for every byte-sized character must round-trip.
    for i in range(256):
        character = chr(i)
        assert evalString(repr(character)) == character

    for invalid in (r"'\x'", r"'\x1'", r"'\xzz'", r"'\x1Z'"):
        try:
            evalString(invalid)
        except ValueError:
            pass
        else:
            raise AssertionError(f"ValueError not raised for {invalid!r}")
